findings.summary: CONFIRMED release blocker: the standard versioned install layout (PluginsPath/ArrTags_<version>) is destroyed by Jellyfin on the next restart once the plugin has written state under its derived data folder PluginsPath/ArrTags, so no ArrTags plugin loads.
findings.detail: Independently reproduced A/B/A against the live pinned host (http://127.0.0.1:8096, /System/Info/Public Version 12.0.0, plugin path /tmp/jf/data/plugins). (A) Extract committed artifacts/ArrTags_0.1.0.0.zip to /tmp/jf/data/plugins/ArrTags_0.1.0.0, restart -> console shows 'Loaded plugin: ArrTags 0.1.0.0', the host writes meta.json (guid 40322d52-5680-449f-b33e-e01836ee2f46, targetAbi 12.0.0.0, status Active), 'Startup complete 0:00:14.7', no ERR/FTL. (B) mkdir -p /tmp/jf/data/plugins/ArrTags/authoritative with sentinel.json, restart -> grep -c 'Loaded plugin: ArrTags' = 0, ArrTags_0.1.0.0 folder is gone while the ArrTags data folder and sentinel survive, 'Startup complete'. (A') rm -rf data/plugins/ArrTags, re-extract the same zip, restart -> 'Loaded plugin: ArrTags 0.1.0.0' again. Root cause in the pinned host source (rev 6c073e19): MediaBrowser.Common/Plugins/BasePluginOfT.cs:50-57 sets DataFolderPath = PluginsPath/Path.GetFileNameWithoutExtension(assemblyFilePath) and the 'append _<version>' branch at line 51 requires 'Version is not null', which is always false during construction because Version is assigned by SetAttributes only afterwards; an independent net10.0 probe referencing the deployed /tmp/jf/jellyfin/MediaBrowser.Common.dll printed 'DataFolderPath = <pluginsPath>/ArrTags' for both a nonexistent and an existing ArrTags directory. Emby.Server.Implementations/Plugins/PluginManager.cs:793-872 (DiscoverPlugins) enumerates every plugins subdirectory, groups entries by manifest Name, sorts by Name then Id then Version (LocalPlugin.Compare), traverses newest-first, and at lines 838-867 deletes the earlier entry's folder whenever a later entry with the same name and non-empty lastName exists; the unversioned Auto-manifest created in LoadManifest (lines 775-786, Id = metafile.GetMD5(), Name = 'ArrTags', Status = Active, supported = true) therefore shadows the real install folder and causes its deletion, after which the data folder is discarded by the final 'DllFiles.Count != 0' filter, yielding zero plugins. The defect hits the supported install flow, not only a manual layout: Emby.Server.Implementations/Updates/InstallationManager.cs:538 + :598 installs to PluginsPath/<package.Name> + '_' + package.Version, i.e. exactly data/plugins/ArrTags_<version>. The plugin's own state root is plugin.DataFolderPath (src/ArrTags/PluginLifecycle/ArrTagsServiceRegistrator.cs:174-183), so any reconciliation/metadata/artwork state write creates data/plugins/ArrTags and triggers the wipe on the subsequent start; the recovery is manual. Phase 7 acceptance criterion 2 is therefore genuinely NOT met, exactly as the worker reported.
evidence: Live A/B/A on /tmp/jf host: 'Loaded plugin: ArrTags 0.1.0.0' (A) -> 0 loads and ArrTags_0.1.0.0 deleted while data/plugins/ArrTags/sentinel.json survives (B) -> loads again after removing data folder (A')
Independent DataFolderPath probe against /tmp/jf/jellyfin/MediaBrowser.Common.dll -> '/tmp/7.2/fakeplugins/ArrTags' for both nonexistent and existing directory
Counter-check that the unversioned layout data/plugins/ArrTags (install folder == data folder) still loads once per restart and preserves the sentinel across restarts
findings.recommended_action: Do not advance to Gate 7; the orchestrator/user must make a production or installation-layout decision before AC2 can be met. Viable directions include a plugin-side workaround (BasePlugin.SetAttributes is public, so the Plugin constructor can install a non-colliding data root, e.g. under PluginsPath/<name>-data or a subdirectory, instead of the auto-derived PluginsPath/<assembly name>), changing the supported install layout to unversioned, and/or an upstream Jellyfin fix to the dead versioned-data-folder branch. The verification task itself should not absorb the production change.

findings.summary: The worker's mechanism explanation is accurate for the observed scenario, and the defect is even more robust than stated: deletion does not depend on the MD5 GUID ordering.
findings.detail: Verified the worker's numeric claim: GetMD5 is new Guid(MD5.HashData(Encoding.Unicode.GetBytes(str))) (MediaBrowser.Common/Extensions/BaseExtensions.cs:30-35); MD5(UTF-16LE 'ArrTags') bytes 30f1a5628e6cdd59cdcc3e1a380fd309 form the .NET Guid 62a5f130-6c8e-59dd-cdcc-3e1a380fd309, which compares greater than the real 40322d52-... GUID. Because the install folder's meta.json (real GUID) and the data folder's Auto-manifest (MD5 GUID) share Name 'ArrTags', LocalPlugin.Compare orders by Id and the data folder is traversed first, so the install folder is deleted - as described. Note additionally that if neither folder has meta.json, both Auto-manifests get the same MD5 GUID and the ordering falls through to Version, where the data folder's _appVersion (12.0.0.0) again exceeds the install folder's version, producing the same deletion. The claim therefore holds and the outcome is not an artifact of a particular GUID ordering. The worker's report is accurate; no correction needed.
findings.recommended_action: None; this strengthens finding 7.2-F1 rather than requiring rework.

findings.summary: The live Plugin.OnUninstalling drain was not exercised (uninstall API requires elevation); the worker disclosed this and it is covered in-process.
findings.detail: Reproduced the API constraint: GET /Plugins and DELETE /Plugins/<guid>/<version> both return HTTP 401 on this host, and Jellyfin.Api/Controllers/PluginsController.cs is annotated [Authorize(Policy = Policies.RequiresElevation)]; StartupWizardCompleted is false, so no authenticated/elevated uninstall is possible in this fixture. The install-folder removal/uninstall lifecycle itself was exercised live (0 loads, clean 'Startup complete'). The worker states the drain remains covered by LifecycleFoundationTests.PluginUninstallHook* and ArtworkLifecycleTests. This is a genuine but bounded residual of the environment, not a verification gap that should block task 7.2.
evidence: Live uninstall: grep -c 'Loaded plugin: ArrTags' = 0, no ArrTags lines, Startup complete
findings.recommended_action: None for 7.2. Re-exercise the live uninstall drain when an authenticated/elevated host or a completed setup wizard is available (naturally owned by a later Phase 7 task).

findings.summary: Live ImageSaver read-back fidelity remains unverified; this is a pre-existing, documented Phase 5 carry-forward rather than a task 7.2 defect.

The worker reports this openly and notes task 5.11's read-back uses a DispatchProxy IProviderManager. research_checked: Pinned Jellyfin source at revision 6c073e19ddf604b2369c638716164fdab4c952dc (shallow clone, 'Bump version to 12.0') reviewed directly: MediaBrowser.Common/Plugins/BasePluginOfT.cs, BasePlugin.cs, LocalPlugin.cs, PluginManifest.cs, IPluginAssembly.cs; Emby.Server.Implementations/Plugins/PluginManager.cs; Emby.Server.Implementations/Updates/InstallationManager.cs; Emby.Server.Implementations/AppBase/BaseApplicationPaths.cs; MediaBrowser.Common/Extensions/BaseExtensions.cs; MediaBrowser.Common/Configuration/IApplicationPaths.cs; Jellyfin.Api/Controllers/PluginsController.cs.

Independent net10.0 probe referencing the deployed /tmp/jf/jellyfin/MediaBrowser.Common.dll (AssemblyName=ArrTags, DispatchProxy IApplicationPaths/IXmlSerializer) printed DataFolderPath = <pluginsPath>/ArrTags for both a nonexistent and an existing ArrTags directory, confirming DataFolderPath is PluginsPath/<DLL file base name> with no _<version> suffix.

MD5/GUID computation: MD5(UTF-16LE 'ArrTags') = 30f1a5628e6cdd59cdcc3e1a380fd309 -> Guid 62a5f130-6c8e-59dd-cdcc-3e1a380fd309 > 40322d52-5680-449f-b33e-e01836ee2f46, matching the worker's claimed value and relative order.

Host layout: PluginsPath = Path.Combine(ProgramDataPath, 'plugins') (BaseApplicationPaths.cs:58) and the live host shows /tmp/jf/data/plugins with the .jellyfin-plugin marker and configurations/ while /tmp/jf/config/plugins does not exist.

Supported install flow: InstallationManager.PerformPackageInstallation installs to PluginsPath/<package.Name> then appends '_' + package.Version (lines 538, 598), confirming the versioned layout is what real repository installs produce.
Jellyfin has no in-process plugin reload; restart is the reload mechanism (PluginManager loads at construction / ApplicationHost startup).
